messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — high GPU queue growth detected for cluster-prod-gpu in us-west-2. Severity: P1. Auto-escalation to oncall-sre. Queue length +4200 over 5m.

oncall-ops: seeing huge enqueue rate, dpq backlog spiking to 18k tokens/s. autoscaler logs show repeated failures to place new pods: "no compatible MIG slice" errors. Impacting hosted API r4 and r5 pools.

sre-jamie: confirmed. Metric snapshots: GPU utilization 98%, pending pods 42, scheduler_throttle_count rising. Latency p95 for text-gen routes jumped 3x, some clients 503ing. Paste of alert link: https://observability/redwood/alerts/5225009876

eng-runtime: quick surface — looks like MIG fragmentation after last night's rolling update. Many hosts are left with 1x16g slices and a bunch of 2x8g reserved; scheduler can't binpack 8g workloads into fragmented slots. Autoscaler tries to create pods but placement fails.

infra-ron: repeating logs from autoscaler: ```ERROR scheduler: cannot place pod default/text-gen-pod-xxxxx: required_mig=[1x8g] available=[nodeA:1x16g, nodeB:2x8g(allocated), nodeC:1x16g(locked)]```

oncall-ops: customers seeing throttling. Support report below.

support-ale: Customer impact: 3 paying customers reported 5xx on production endpoints. Top affected: Acme Analytics (high throughput batch), Novaflow (chat). Support tickets: #4332 #4333 #4334. Notified account leads. Customers experiencing timeouts and error spikes between 16:02-16:18 UTC.

eng-runtime: mitigation options — 1) enable burstpool for r5 (temporary relax binpacking) 2) kick a manual repack job to evict low priority pods and consolidate MIG sizes 3) create a hotfix: allow scheduler to fallback to 16g-placement for 8g workloads until repack completes. Prefer 2 then 1 as fallback.

sre-jamie: timeline: need something in next 10-15m. Can we run repack now? Any risk to live traffic?

eng-runtime: risk: repack will evict low-priority batches; multi-tenant high-priority can be safe if we mark them protected. We'll run in waves and monitor queue. Command we'll run from controller host: ```/opt/inference/bin/repack --cluster cluster-prod-gpu --dry-run=false --evict-label=evictable --concurrency=4```

infra-ron: starting repack, wave 1. I'm also enabling burstpool as emergency fallback while repack proceeds: ```rbacctl patch config autopool --set burstpool.enabled=true --namespace=infra``` will give short-term capacity by oversubscribing lower-priority nodes.

incident-bot: NOTE: burstpool enabled by infra-ron at 16:07:12 UTC. Auto-notification to billing-disabled to avoid unexpected cost surge.

support-ale: update from customers: Acme still seeing intermittent 503s. Novaflow reports degraded quality but queue draining slowly.

eng-runtime: repack wave 1 completed. Observed ~12 evictions, freed 4x8g-equivalent slots. Scheduler now places 6 pending pods. queue length dropped 28% in 4m.

sre-jamie: metrics: pending pods -> 12, gpu-util -> 92%, p95 latency trending down. But autoscaler still logging "fragmentation: unable to satisfy placement" for some requests. Looks like MIG size mismatch persists on subset of nodes.

infra-ron: I identified a cluster of nodes (pool-b) with mixed MIG configs from previous upgrades. Those nodes have 3x8g slices partially allocated; they can't accept new 8g pods because NVML reports slices in use by leftover system pods. Running `kubectl get pods -o wide -n kube-system` shows helper jobs pinned to the slices.

eng-runtime: plan: 1) cordon those 6 nodes in pool-b, 2) evict non-prod jobs, 3) force a MIG resize sequence via node-agent: ```node-agent --node pool-b-0 --set-mig 2x8g && node-agent --node pool-b-1 --set-mig 1x16g``` — will need rolling restarts. Doing this during low risk windows but we're past that. Request oncall approval to proceed with rolling MIG resize.

oncall-ops: approved. Make sure to exclude premium customer pods from eviction; tag them with `slo:protected`. Also coordinate with support for customer comms.

support-ale: notifying affected accounts now: "We are actively mitigating GPU placement issues; some requests may see degraded perf for up to 30 minutes." CC: account teams.

product-nora: please put a short customer-facing note in status page if we cross 30m. Keep me posted on ACME/Novaflow.

eng-runtime: kicking MIG resize on pool-b-0 -> pool-b-3 sequence. Will do one node at a time. Command logs: ```[16:15:43] node-agent: starting mig resize pool-b-0 -> 2x8g
[16:15:46] node-agent: drain pods with label evictable
[16:15:58] node-agent: apply MIG config
[16:16:10] node-agent: node back online
```

infra-ron: after resizing two nodes, observed immediate placement success for 9 pending pods. queue length down to pre-incident baseline. I am pausing further resizes to monitor.

support-ale: Acme confirms calls returning to normal, Novaflow reporting improved latencies. Tickets updated.

sre-jamie: monitoring for regression. Autoscaler logs cleared earlier "no compatible MIG slice" error messages. For root cause we need to trace last night's rolling update that left inconsistent MIG configs.

eng-runtime: immediate mitigations summary: repack -> freed slots, burstpool -> temporary oversubscribe, targeted MIG resizes -> fixed fragmented nodes. Next: revert burstpool, revert eviction flags, and run a cluster-wide MIG audit + a safe repack job.

oncall-ops: revert burstpool now? Cost vs risk? If traffic steady, revert in 10m.

infra-ron: scheduled revert in 12m. Will also submit infra task to add pre-check to rolling updates to verify MIG uniformity.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigated. Severity downgraded to P2 at 16:38:20 UTC. Will close after postmortem and follow-ups assigned.

product-nora: good work. please include customer impact window and list of affected accounts in the postmortem.

eng-runtime: handoff to eng-runtime for postmortem. Action items I'll own: - run cluster MIG audit script and produce CSV of node->mig config - add autoscaler better failure metrics and a fallback routing rule - write repack runbook with safe disruption windows.

sre-jamie: I'll own monitoring alerts tuning and add a dashboard that surfaces fragmentation heatmap.

infra-ron: I'll add preflight checks to rolling-update pipeline and prune orphaned system pods that can hold MIG slices.

support-ale: I'll finish customer follow-ups and escalate any billing credits if needed.

incident-bot: HANDOFF: oncall-ops -> eng-runtime at 16:42:00 UTC. Postmortem task created: https://projects/redwood/pm/INC-5225009876

eng-runtime: final note: initial cause appears to be a combination of (a) rolling update that left mixed MIG shapes in pool-b, (b) autoscaler lacked a fallback placement policy, and (c) no preflight MIG uniformity check. Will avoid repeating by adding preflight + repack scheduling.

oncall-ops: thanks all. if anyone sees regression ping this thread. :thumbsup:
